identity.real_world_identity_notes: Marque-specialist evidence specifies a six-speed sequential gearbox with ignition cut for the 2004-2005 996 GT3 RSR. AMS2 cockpit inspection confirms sequential-stick actuation without paddles.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a round rim without an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car stalled when moving from rest without physical clutch input.
All six sequential-stick gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts with automatic throttle cut.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted and an automatic throttle blip was observed.
The opened historical source does not independently establish the downshift automation or start technique.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Standing-start clutch, six-speed sequential stick without paddles, automatic cut and blip, and round no-display rim were directly observed.
The automatic blip was re-measured on 2026-08-18 in AMS2 1.6.9.91, observation ams2.porsche-996-gt3-rsr.20260818t040508728z-3d936a61, and held under the corrected measurement: the spike is the car's.

confidence.basis: Exact simulator identity, modeled cockpit hardware, and shift behavior were directly tested; specialist historical evidence independently supports the six-speed sequential gearbox and ignition cut.

Contemporary 2004 Alex Job Racing material names the 2004 Porsche 911 GT3 RSR and supplies its race specification. Stuttcars independently scopes the 996 RSR to the 2004-2005 seasons and identifies the internal generation as 996. The PMR attachment supplies the matching telemetry name and N-GT class; it is used only to connect the observation to the real-car identity, not to establish real-car technique.

claims.basis: Official release context and exact live CarModel/class observation establish the simulated identity.
Specialist historical evidence and direct exercise of the modeled six-speed sequential stick with automatic cut agree.
Direct current-game tests and cockpit inspection establish the start clutch, automatic blip, and round no-display rim.
The 2004 team specification says dog type, straight-cut transmission; Porsche independently calls it a sequential jaw-type gearbox.
The clear cockpit photograph shows fixed hand grips around a central button/control face rather than a continuous circular band. Under the data-model definition this is gt-formula.

Contemporary team data and Porsche's technical summary both specify six forward gears. The 2004 team specification says dog type, straight-cut transmission; Porsche independently calls it a sequential jaw-type gearbox. The period Alex Job Racing photograph is captioned as showing the sequential gear shift, the specification names an in-line shift mechanism, and the later onboard description identifies a push-pull cockpit lever. No source supports steering-wheel paddles for this target. Both sources explicitly describe a sequential gearbox; the team source also identifies the in-line shift mechanism. The period specification documents sensor-controlled traction interruption, and the model history explicitly says the ignition cut enables shifts at full throttle. The documented sensor-controlled traction interruption is an automatic power cut associated with the shift mechanism; the independent description calls it ignition cut. Manual blip is a downshift action in this data model; no upshift-blip procedure is being asserted. Automatic blip is a downshift action in this data model; the documented upshift system is interruption/cut, not a blip. Throttle lift is recorded as an upshift action in this data model; no separate downshift-lift claim is made. The documented interruption is an upshift function; no downshift cut is established. The clear cockpit photograph shows fixed hand grips around a central button/control face rather than a continuous circular band. Under the data-model definition this is gt-formula. The wheel is a fixed-grip gt-formula control-face design; open_top is therefore not-applicable under the schema rather than a round/d-shaped rim yes/no property. The photograph nevertheless visibly shows the upper rim opening. The wheel face in the clear photograph contains controls but no display; the contemporary team specification places the MoTeC display in the electrical/dashboard system behind the wheel. The full-width photograph shows no light array on the wheel; the visible light strip is on the dashboard behind it. This is limited to the photographed restored configuration and does not claim that no 996 RSR ever used a different wheel. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip.

deviations.basis: The exact 2004-2005 996 GT3 RSR evidence establishes a dogbox, whereas the archetype describes a sequential gearbox.

driver_summary: Sequential stick, one gear at a time. The car cuts the upshift and blips the downshift itself, so once you are rolling the gearbox asks nothing of your feet.
